findings.bug: ReplayEngine._flatten / _reset_book close every open position against self._bar, the last bar processed. On the V11 tape that is BTCUSDT's bar at the end of a replay, so the execution model charges an alt's exit BTC's half tick + 0.02 x BTC's ATR in the alt's price units: 1.55 USD per coin on a 5m position, 10.02 USD on a 1h position. ARB at 0.2018 was 'sold' at -1.348. The exit is labelled 'time' ('end of replay'), so studies that only drop 'reset' kept it. Live trading never takes this path.
findings.how_checked: 32 replays (38 study results) through each study's own run() with in-memory instrumentation only; study-time parameters restored (V11.3 min stop 0.6%, V11.1/V11.2 0.8%); 38 of 38 'orig' results identical to the published JSON. fixed = end-of-replay trades dropped (V13's rule); repriced = kept but priced on the coin's own last bar.
findings.bogus_trades: Only where a position was still open at 2026-09-28 23:59 UTC: 4 of 32 replays had a damaging one. V11.3 MAKER_TP+MINSTOP15: ARB -123.7 R (own bar +0.76). V11.3 MAKER_TP+MINSTOP20: ARB -281.4 R (own bar +0.63), UNI -1.81 R (+0.79). V11.4 hold X4 / NONE: LIT -61.7 R (-0.09), LINK -14.3 / -13.4 R (-0.50 / -0.35). Harmless: HYPE in V11.3 MINSTOP10 and MAKER_TP+MINSTOP10 (+0.28 / +0.32 R instead of +0.80 / +0.84). All V11.1 and V11.2 runs and every other V11.3 / V11.4 run: none.
findings.decision_changed: V11.3 Zap wider-stop follow-up (rule: a wider stop replaces 1.0% only if better in BOTH halves). Recorded: 1.5% and 2.0% rejected, 'worse than 1.0% in half 2' (-0.103 / -0.149 vs -0.098). That was the ARB trade. Corrected half 2: -0.066 (1.5%) and -0.055 (2.0%) vs -0.098; both pass, and the rule picks 2.0%: -0.042 / -0.055 / -0.049 R per trade (half 1 / half 2 / all) vs -0.130 / -0.098 / -0.114 at 1.0%, net -53.9 vs -163.9 USDT over 90 days. Still a loss: it cuts cost, it is not an edge.
findings.decisions_unchanged: Resting take-profits (MAKER_TP) for all four scanners; V11.3 1.0% over 0.6% (main Zap run); STRICT5 and TOP2 rejected; Juno 1.2% and Kilo 1.5% minimum stops and TOP2 rejected (no bogus trades in any V11.1 / V11.2 run); hold-study rule outcomes V11.1 X1, V11.2 X2, V11.3 NONE, V11.4 X1.
findings.numbers_that_were_wrong_without_a_decisi: V11.4 longer holds looked far worse in half 2 because of LIT / LINK: X4 -0.131 -> -0.070, NONE -0.160 -> -0.068 (X1 -0.062). Still worse than X1 in half 2, so the rule keeps X1, but on the whole window X4 (-0.058) and NONE (-0.044) are slightly BETTER than X1 (-0.060): 'holding longer is worse' for V11.4 was overstated.
findings.resets: Only the hold study counts reset exits. They are priced on 1000PEPEUSDT's bar (the first coin of the new day): 0.2-1.7 bp of slippage instead of the coin's own 1.4-5.2 bp, about 0.01 R per reset trade too good, at most 0.002 R per trade on any hold result. No decision changes.
findings.not_rerun: Studies that chose on the DISCOVERY half (ladder rungs, equal spacing, TP1 share / lock, level fills, spacing, breakout stop) cannot change: an end-of-replay trade opens on the tape's last day (2026-09-28), the discovery half ends 2026-08-15. Their reported confirmation / whole-window numbers may still carry such a trade. Informational runs (activity check, gap guard, exit fixes, live exits) were not rerun.
findings.live: Live and paper-forward bots are unaffected. Zap runs live with the 1.0% minimum stop; moving it to 2.0% is a V11 code change (CapParams), i.e. a re-freeze and a new experiment -- the operator's call, not done here.
